timeline: You might think earthquakes only shake the ground, but the 1950 Assam shock triggered massive landslides and surface ruptures that drastically altered the Himalayan landscape.
On August fifteenth, a massive magnitude eight point six shock struck.
It remains the largest onshore earthquake ever recorded from continental collision.
Enormous landslides choked river valleys across the rugged Mishmi Hills.
The debris dammed waterways so severely that rivers physically reversed their flow.
Behind one mud barrier, a colossal lake swelled for eight silent days.
A seven meter wall of water rushed down and submerged nearby villages.
When the shaking finally stopped, nearly four thousand eight hundred lives were lost.
Pilots flying overhead reported mountains completely out of their former positions.
Even soundwaves traveled across the globe, recorded as far away as Europe.
You assume earthquakes only shake the ground, but the 1950 Assam quake physically rearranged the Himalayan landscape.
